title: The Testimony Of The Heavens 1st Degree The Heavens As The Page Of Divine Unity

questions.question: What is the title of this passage?
questions.answer: The Supreme Sign.

questions.question: Who is asking questions in this passage?
questions.answer: A traveler.

questions.question: What is the traveler asking the universe about?
questions.answer: His Maker.

questions.question: What do the seven heavens, the earth, and everything in them do for Allah?
questions.answer: They praise and glorify Him.

questions.question: What does the verse say people do not understand well?
questions.answer: How all things praise Allah.

questions.question: Which part of creation is mentioned first after the verse?
questions.answer: The heavens.

questions.question: Why does the passage begin with the heavens?
questions.answer: Because they clearly point to Allah and people look at them with wonder.

questions.question: What does the world seem like to a person who arrives in it?
questions.answer: A welcoming place full of lessons, beauty, and wisdom.

questions.question: What two big questions does the traveler ask about the world?
questions.answer: Who made it and who rules it.

questions.question: What does the traveler first see when looking for the answer?
questions.answer: The sky with the stars.

questions.question: What does the sky seem to say to the traveler?
questions.answer: To look at it for guidance.

questions.question: What amazing thing does the traveler notice about the heavenly bodies?
questions.answer: They stay up without pillars and move very fast in order.

questions.question: What do the heavenly bodies not do, even though they move quickly?
questions.answer: They do not crash into each other.

questions.question: Which two great bodies are given their own jobs?
questions.answer: The sun and the moon.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the way everything in the heavens is managed?
questions.answer: It is managed all at once, strongly, and without mistakes.

questions.question: What happens to the dirt and waste of the heavens?
questions.answer: It is cleaned away.

questions.question: What picture is used for the moving heavenly bodies?
questions.answer: A well-ordered army.

questions.question: What picture is used for the changing night sky?
questions.answer: A screen showing new scenes.

questions.question: What main idea do these signs in the heavens teach the traveler?
questions.answer: Allah is powerful, wise, and in control.

questions.question: In this passage, what is the traveler trying to find out?
questions.answer: Who his Maker is.

questions.question: What words begin the passage in a blessed way?
questions.answer: In the Name of Allah, the Merciful, the Compassionate.

questions.question: According to the verse, how much of creation praises Allah?
questions.answer: All of it.

questions.question: What are the two qualities of Allah named at the end of the verse?
questions.answer: He is Forebearing and Forgiving.

questions.question: What does the passage say many people feel when they look at the heavens?
questions.answer: Wonder and joy.

questions.question: Why are the heavens a good place to begin looking?
questions.answer: They openly show signs of Allah’s oneness.

questions.question: How is the world described for the traveler?
questions.answer: Like a place of welcome, learning, and careful planning.

questions.question: Besides asking who made the world, what else does the traveler wonder?
questions.answer: Who is the ruler of this great world.

questions.question: What beautiful part of the sky is especially noticed?
questions.answer: The stars.

questions.question: What does the traveler learn from watching the sky carefully?
questions.answer: Great order and control are there.

questions.question: How are some heavenly bodies compared to the earth?
questions.answer: Some are much heavier than the earth.

questions.question: How do the heavenly bodies move?
questions.answer: Very fast and together in harmony.

questions.question: What shows that their movement is controlled and not wild?
questions.answer: They keep their order and do not collide.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the lights in the sky?
questions.answer: They keep shining without fuel like earthly lamps need.

questions.question: What does it mean that the sun and moon do not rebel?
questions.answer: They obey the jobs given to them.

questions.question: How much space is being managed in the heavens?
questions.answer: An immeasurably vast space.

questions.question: What happens to the earth that changes what we see in the sky?
questions.answer: The earth turns.

questions.question: Because the earth turns, how does the sky look to us?
questions.answer: It appears in different forms at night and through the year.

questions.question: What does all this order help the traveler understand about Allah?
questions.answer: Allah has great power, wisdom, and rule over creation.

questions.question: What kind of person is the main figure in this passage?
questions.answer: A traveler who asks questions.

questions.question: What is he asking creation to show him?
questions.answer: The One who made him and the world.

questions.question: What does the Qur’an verse say about things in the heavens and earth?
questions.answer: They all glorify Allah.

questions.question: What is hard for people to grasp about that glorifying?
questions.answer: The way it happens.

questions.question: After the verse, what part of creation does the passage focus on first?
questions.answer: The heavens.

questions.question: What makes the heavens special for all people to look at?
questions.answer: They are always visible and fill people with amazement.

questions.question: What are some ways the world is described to the traveler?
questions.answer: Like a feast, an exhibit, a camp, a playground, and a school.

questions.question: What does the traveler want to know about this “great book” of the world?
questions.answer: Who wrote it.

questions.question: What appears to him first as a sign?
questions.answer: The star-filled sky.

questions.question: What invitation does the sky seem to give?
questions.answer: To study it and be guided.

questions.question: What holds the heavenly bodies up?
questions.answer: Allah’s power, not pillars.

questions.question: What is surprising about the speed of the heavenly bodies?
questions.answer: They move extremely fast.

questions.question: Even with so many bodies moving fast, what problem does not happen?
questions.answer: They do not strike one another.

questions.question: What does the passage say about disorder in the heavens?
questions.answer: There is no disorder in how they are handled.

questions.question: What does the passage say about managing everything at the same time?
questions.answer: It is done equally and completely without anything being missed.

questions.question: How are strong powers in the heavens treated?
questions.answer: They are made to obey.

questions.question: What is done to keep the heavens pure?
questions.answer: Their waste is cleared away.

questions.question: What does comparing the heavens to an army teach us?
questions.answer: Their movement is disciplined and under command.

questions.question: What lesson does the changing sky teach the traveler?
questions.answer: The One in control can show endless wise and beautiful scenes.

questions.question: What is the name of the section the passage begins with?
questions.answer: The Supreme Sign.

questions.question: What does the traveler want to learn from the universe?
questions.answer: Who his Lord and Maker is.

questions.question: In the verse, who praises Allah besides the heavens?
questions.answer: The earth and everything in them.

questions.question: What do people fail to fully understand, according to the verse?
questions.answer: The praising of creation.

questions.question: Why are the heavens mentioned before other things?
questions.answer: They are a shining sign of Allah’s unity.

questions.question: How does the traveler see the world at first?
questions.answer: As a generous and amazing place.

questions.question: What questions come to his mind about the world?
questions.answer: Who made it and who rules it.

questions.question: What part of the heavens catches his attention first?
questions.answer: The stars spread across the sky.

questions.question: What does the traveler do after the sky seems to call him?
questions.answer: He looks closely at it.

questions.question: Name one thing the passage says is happening in the heavens.
questions.answer: Huge bodies are being kept in place and moved in order.

questions.question: What is unusual about those huge bodies?
questions.answer: Some are much bigger than the earth and move very quickly.

questions.question: What shows mercy and wisdom in the heavens’ movement?
questions.answer: Everything works together without crashing or confusion.

questions.question: What jobs are the sun and moon given?
questions.answer: Each has its own duty.

questions.question: How carefully is the huge space above managed?
questions.answer: With complete control and no lack.

questions.question: What happens to harmful leftovers in the heavens?
questions.answer: They are cleaned off.

questions.question: How are the heavenly bodies like soldiers?
questions.answer: They move in a trained and obedient way.

questions.question: What makes the sky look different at different times?
questions.answer: The turning of the earth.

questions.question: If a second grader told the main lesson simply, what could he say?
questions.answer: The sky shows that Allah wisely controls everything.

questions.question: What does the passage call the traveler’s search?
questions.answer: A questioning of the universe about his Maker.

questions.question: What truth from the verse covers all created things?
questions.answer: Everything praises Allah.

questions.question: Does the verse say people fully understand that praise, or not fully?
questions.answer: Not fully.

questions.question: What is the first created thing the passage studies?
questions.answer: The heavens.

questions.question: Why do the heavens make a strong sign for people?
questions.answer: Everyone can look at them and see their beauty and order.

questions.question: What kind of place does the world seem to be for a visitor?
questions.answer: A rich, wise, and wonderful place.

questions.question: What does the traveler wonder about the “book” of the world?
questions.answer: Who its author is.

questions.question: What seems to invite him to search for the answer?
questions.answer: The face of the sky filled with stars.

questions.question: What does he notice about the support of the heavenly bodies?
questions.answer: They stay up without columns.

questions.question: What does he notice about their movement?
questions.answer: It is fast, balanced, and orderly.

questions.question: What danger is avoided in their movement?
questions.answer: Crashing into one another.

questions.question: What is amazing about the lights in the heavens?
questions.answer: They keep burning without oil.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the control of the heavens in huge space?
questions.answer: Everything is directed together in one way without weakness or missing anything.

questions.question: What happens to wild strength in the heavenly bodies?
questions.answer: It is made obedient to a law.

questions.question: What cleaning work is done in the heavens?
questions.answer: Refuse is removed from them.

questions.question: What comparison helps us imagine the heavens moving in order?
questions.answer: Soldiers marching under command.

questions.question: What comparison helps us imagine how the sky changes before us?
questions.answer: A screen showing scenes.

questions.question: What can the traveler infer from all these signs?
questions.answer: The Maker of the heavens is powerful, wise, and perfect in control.

questions.question: What is the passage mainly about?
questions.answer: Looking at the universe to learn about Allah.

questions.question: Who is the person thinking and observing in the passage?
questions.answer: A traveler.

questions.question: What does the verse say the seven heavens and the earth do?
questions.answer: They glorify and praise Allah.

questions.question: What does the verse teach about our understanding of that praise?
questions.answer: We do not truly understand it well.

questions.question: What part of creation is chosen as the first sign to study?
questions.answer: The heavens.

questions.question: What does the passage say the heavens are like for people to see?
questions.answer: A bright page that shows Allah’s oneness.

questions.question: What kinds of places is the world compared to?
questions.answer: A banquet, an exhibit, a camp, a place of fun, and a place of learning.

questions.question: What is one reason the traveler feels amazed in the world?
questions.answer: It is full of wisdom and beauty.

questions.question: What does he want to know about the ruler of this world?
questions.answer: Who that ruler is.

questions.question: What part of the heavens speaks to him in a figurative way?
questions.answer: The starry sky.

questions.question: What does the traveler learn when he looks at the heavens?
questions.answer: They are being run with order and purpose.

questions.question: How are the heavenly bodies kept above?
questions.answer: Without visible supports.

questions.question: How can we tell their motion is controlled?
questions.answer: They move quickly together and still do not hit one another.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the sun and moon?
questions.answer: They each do their assigned work.

questions.question: How much of the heavens is under control?
questions.answer: All of it, even the vast space beyond measure.

questions.question: What does the passage say about mistakes or shortages in this management?
questions.answer: There are none.

questions.question: What is done with unwanted matter in the heavens?
questions.answer: It is cleared away.

questions.question: Why is the example of an army used?
questions.answer: To show discipline, order, and obedience.

questions.question: Why is the example of a screen used?
questions.answer: To show the sky appears in changing scenes over time.

questions.question: What is the best short conclusion from the whole passage?
questions.answer: The heavens clearly show Allah’s greatness and careful control.
